match.reason: The bank point covers internal versus external recruitment in general, but the new point is about specific sources of applicants such as the intranet, word of mouth, websites, agencies and social media, which the card does not teach, so adding them would be a new idea rather than a small change.

draft.title: Recruitment
card: Recruitment is finding people who might apply for a job. It happens before the business chooses among them.

looking for applicants already in the business, through the intranet (the business's private network) or word of mouth. It is usually quicker and cheaper, and the business already knows the person. The pool of applicants is small, and it leaves a gap in the old role.

looking for applicants outside the business, through job websites, recruitment agencies and social media. It reaches many people and can bring in new ideas. It can cost more and take longer, and the business knows less about each person.
A business weighs these pros and cons against the job. Agencies charge a fee, but they can do much of the searching for the business.
draft.remember: Internal is cheaper and better known but narrow. External reaches wider but costs more.

a.q: Which is a limit of recruiting internally, rather than externally?
opts: Only people already in the business can apply
The business knows little about each applicant
It usually costs more than advertising widely
It cannot be done through the intranet
a.why: Internal recruitment draws only on current staff, so the pool is small. The business knows its own staff well, and it is usually cheaper, so the other options describe external recruitment or are wrong.
a.clue: Think about who is able to see an internal notice.

b.q: Priya's bakery in Geelong needs a manager with new ideas for online sales, and no current staff have this skill. Which method suits best?
opts: Advertising on job websites and social media
Posting the job on the bakery's intranet
Asking current staff to mention it by word of mouth
Promoting the bakery's most senior baker
b.why: Only external methods can reach people with skills the bakery lacks, and websites and social media reach many people. The intranet and word of mouth are internal, so they would draw mainly on current staff, who lack the skill.
b.clue: Where would people with skills the bakery lacks be found?

a.best: Only people already in the business can apply

b.best: Advertising on job websites and social media
